chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: New Year's night at Small's Paradise: the ice bowl charge
summary: Buck, Bubbles and their wives go to Ed Small's Paradise, balk at the $20 charge and prices, and are accused of breaking a bowl.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Getting back to a point I'd like you to know about is that when Buck was a little fella he was all right, but when he got to New York he got to foolin' around with the people in Harlem and he got uncontrollable and I couldn't do much with him. I'd leave him go one way and I'd go another.

We got in a big fight uptown in a club for the first time we got into a big fight. His wife, my wife and him and I all went to Small's Paradise on New Year's night, that was it. Then going in the club -- and I had already been going to another club owned by this same man, Ed Small, over at 5th Avenue and 135th Street, down in a hole, called Small's. But now Small's Paradise, he made a nightclub and I used to come over to the nightclub and watch the

entertainment on the strength of being in the hole with him when he first started, but never asked for nothin'. But I'd do this for nothin', sing, dance for him and when he got this -- the first New Year's party we went out to in his nightclub, Small's Paradise, he wanted to charge us -- it cost $20 a person to get in. Then they didn't charge the price, then he wanted to raise the ginger ale and Coca Cola stuff and ice. I think he sat a bowl of ice on the table when we got in in the amount of two and a half for the bowl of ice and a dollar and a quarter for a pint of ginger ale or two and a half for a pint of ginger ale, something like that.

However, I thought it was too much so we're going to leave there, we're not going to stay there. So -- just take it back. So he took it back and when he got it back he went and told -- I had to tell Ed Small that we broke the ice bowl. Now, George, if I broke an ice bowl it only cost a dollar and a half for a bowl.
